tag: Episode 28 · The Room I Came Back To
title: The Room I Came Back To

beats.t: When Yeoni opened their eyes, a familiar stain marked the ceiling. Where rain leaked. Their room.
It was still dark outside. Rain tapped the window. Their body felt heavy, like someone waking from a long dream.
This... is my room? My actual room?
They raised a hand. No pink hoof. Five fingers. A little flour beneath the nails.
(Bakery flour. It wasn't a dream.)
The phone beside the pillow lit up. The date was only one night later. All the time spent circling five islands, one night.
[ Code Destiny · Destiny code 8/8 · Return complete ]
One night? Do you know how much bread I ate over there? All of that in one night?
Fabric brushed beside the bed. Neo sat in a chair. Silver hair and deep navy clothes. The same human form Yeoni had seen on the river.
...Neo? You're Neo, right?
Neo stretched stiff shoulders, as though he'd sat there all night. Then spoke in his usual businesslike tone.
“Customer Support. On your first morning after returning, are you experiencing any difficulties?”
You came back with me. You really came all the way here?
“Other people can see me here, too. So don't call me Customer Support outside. Awkward to explain.”
I was always a little weird. You're just making me weirder.
“Still the same form. Though that doesn't mean I have an ID. Quite a lot to explain.”
Yeoni carefully held Neo's wrist. His hand was warm. Beneath his left sleeve, the rust-colored wound from the river remained.
A human hand. Still feels amazing.
“You had hooves until yesterday, too. Let's not get too amazed at each other.”
So tell me if it hurts. Becoming human doesn't change the promise.
“I know. Hard to hide it when checking my hand is the first thing you do.”
Even as he spoke, Neo did not pull away. Instead, he briefly closed his fingers around Yeoni's.
As the sun rose, the room revealed itself. Piled assignments, a dried-out plant, and an umbrella shoved into a corner.
The umbrella was inside out, two ribs broken. Just as the wind had left it the night before Yeoni went to the other world.
(That day really was the worst. Umbrella flipped, bus missed, angry ratings posted.)
A card lay facedown beside the umbrella. Who knew how long it had been there. A small star pattern marked its back.
What's this card? Was it always in my home?
Yeoni tried turning it over. It slipped from their fingers. No matter how often they tried, it would not turn. As though the time had not yet come.
“That card is yours. It'll turn when you're ready. Leave it for now.”
Customer Support always saves the important things for later. One star deducted.
Instead of the card, Yeoni picked up the umbrella. They taped the broken ribs and slowly straightened the bent ones by hand. Not pulling. Pushing.
If it's flipped, fix it. Don't throw it away.
The umbrella opened. A little crooked, but it would keep out rain. Yeoni liked it.
A paper bag rested on the desk. The bread Luna had pressed into their arms at the door. Still warm.
Luna's bread. I really brought it back. Really.
One bite spread the scent of butter through the room. Yeoni remembered the words: fortune could be taken, appetite could not.
A folded sheet came from the bag's bottom. A brush-drawn crescent and unreadable characters.
(What's this? Not a receipt. Not Luna's sister's handwriting.)
“A talisman. I can smell it. Smells of a compatibility con artist.”
Yundal? When did he slip this in?
The paper would not unfold. Trying to force it made Yeoni's fingertips sting. They tucked it, still folded, inside their wallet.
I'll definitely ask him later. If there's a way back.
“The door's closed. No way back right now.” Neo looked outside. The hand on his knee slowly stiffened.
The trip to school was strangely smooth. The bus came on time, with a front seat empty.
A coin in the vending machine brought down two drinks. Even though Yeoni was late, the professor smiled and marked them present.
Weird. So weird. Nobody stepped on my foot today.
Outside the classroom, a classmate caught Yeoni. They thought the group-project materials were lost, but Yeoni's file alone had survived intact.
Only my file? Usually mine is the first one to vanish. That's practically a law of nature.
The classmate looked at Yeoni like a savior. Yeoni smiled awkwardly. Being the one praised was unfamiliar.
Guess I'm lucky today. Should I buy a lottery ticket?
The phone in their bag vibrated. One line appeared in the message preview. No sender.
“Customer Support. Lottery tickets are not recommended. That's not how you use fortune.”
(When did he send a message? And how does he know my phone password?)
Won't even let me dream. Another star deducted.
Yeoni's bad luck had always been diligent. Showed up to work every day without fail. Today, it was absent without notice.
(Because it's 8/8? Once the code is complete, does luck become normal, too?)
At lunch, Yeoni ate half a roll on a bench. They saved the rest. Somehow, it felt as though they would give it to someone.
Not dieting. Just wanted to save half. Respect for the bread, maybe.
Then a raindrop fell from the clear sky onto the back of Yeoni's hand. Cold. Looking up, they saw not a single cloud.
(The smell of rain.)
Yeoni knew it. A smell from somewhere before. By the river, and from a wet cloak.
Must be my imagination. It's summer. Summer has lots of smells.
But the drop on their hand did not dry for a long time.
Yeoni returned the remaining half-roll to the bag. They didn't know who it was for. Half simply felt like someone's share.
Learned that over there. Bread doubles when you share it. Luna's sister said so.
By evening, real rain fell. A fluorescent light flickered in the apartment corridor.
Moving boxes stood outside the home next door. It had been vacant a long time.
A black umbrella rested before its door. There since last night. Water still dripped from its tip.
(That umbrella was there last night, too. It moved in before the boxes.)
A mover set down the last box and asked for a signature. A woman in a black coat signed, her back turned.
Wet hair spilled over her collar. Tall. Her signing hand moved strangely slowly. Stroke by stroke, like writing in a ledger.
Hello, I'm next door. Moving in the rain must have been hard.
The woman's shoulders stiffened for an instant. She did not turn.
Yes. Thank you. Sorry for the noise.
A brief, polite voice. Its ending was cool. Like rainwater.
Then the door behind Yeoni opened. Neo came out and stopped beside them.
Neo's gaze fixed on the woman's right wrist. He half stepped in front of Yeoni. Lips about to offer a greeting shut tight.
Neo! What's wrong? She's our neighbor. Sorry, he's not usually like this.
It's all right. Your companion seems a little wary of me.
The woman never showed her face. Taking the black umbrella, she went inside.
The door closed. Only the smell of rain remained. Exactly the smell from the drop on Yeoni's hand that afternoon.
That night, Neo did not sleep. Sitting on the windowsill, he stared only at the wall.
(I've never seen him this guarded. Not even when he was a cat.)
Neo. Why don't you like her? You haven't even seen her face.
“I don't know. There's a smell. I've smelled it somewhere, but I can't remember.”
You can't remember? Customer Support?
“Things from there blur here. Yundal said it. They might fade like a dream.”
Yeoni pulled up the blanket. The words were frightening. Luna's smile, Moka's sharp tongue, the tiger's red eyes. Their edges were already blurring.
Yeoni opened the phone's notes and wrote whatever came to mind. Bread. Luna. Moka. Yundal. Black tiger.
Can't forget. Writing it down should keep it from blurring so much.
Their fingers faltered. Nothing came after tiger. The drumming child's name. They had definitely seen it, but the shapes were blurred as if by water.
I can't remember the child's name. I saw it inside that cloak.
“The tiger has it. Not knowing it doesn't make it disappear.”
(The tiger has it. Write that down, too.)
Yeoni added a line. Drum boy's name, inside tiger's cloak. Then a small question mark beside it.
“...Good habit. Five stars.” Neo's voice softened a little.
First time I've seen Customer Support rate the customer.
No sound came from beyond the wall. Someone lived there, yet there wasn't even a breath.
Then the phone screen flickered. A black dot spread in the app icon's corner. Like a moon covering the sun.
[ Checking connection · · · ]
When Yeoni looked again, the dot was gone. Only the rain continued. On the windowsill, Neo never took his eyes from the wall.
